newsitem.title: USA: USDA 'resolute' if no meat deal with EU - Glickman.
newsitem.headline: USDA 'resolute' if no meat deal with EU - Glickman.

text.p: The United States is resolute in its plans to curtail meat shipments from the European Union if there is no agreement on meat inspection rules, Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Tuesday.
"We are resolute. We have to respond with clarity," Glickman told Reuters following a breakfast speech. "I still hope we can work something out in the next week."
U.S. and EU negotiators were due to hold their second day of talks Tuesday on the so-called veterinary equivalency issue.
The EU has said it will implement new veterinary and sanitary controls beginning April 1.
USDA has said it would retaliate for any cutback in access to EU markets caused by the new rules.

Several hundred million dollars in beef, pork and poultry exports were at stake in the discussions being held in Washington. An agreement on mutual recognition of standards would allow each side to accept meat from the other even if they disagree on particulars of how to assure the meat is safe.
